defects.justification: The public-IP check (line 77) resolves the hostname separately from the actual connect in opener.open, so DNS rebinding (or a multi-A record) lets a create request make the server fetch an internal/metadata address; the README admits this. Fix by connecting to the validated IP (or re-checking the peer address).

Only URLError/OSError/ValueError/LookupError are caught; http.client.HTTPException subclasses such as IncompleteRead or LineTooLong from a hostile target server propagate and turn link creation into a 500 instead of the documented 'title is null' behaviour.
`with sqlite3.connect(...)` only commits/rolls back; it does not close the connection, so every create_app call leaks a SQLite handle (should use contextlib.closing or call close()).
No MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is configured, so request.get_json reads an arbitrarily large request body into memory; the 256 KiB cap only applies to the fetched page, not to incoming requests.
Dependencies use open-ended `>=` ranges (flask>=3.0, pytest>=8.0), so builds are not reproducible and can pick up breaking or compromised releases.
